Compose_HealthColor.description: Business-ready badge color: green=all clear, amber=temporary issues (auto-retrying), red=needs finance/accounting attention. Kept as a single source of truth here (not duplicated per caller) so both the scheduled daily digest and the immediate on-demand digest always render identically.

Compose_SummaryMessage.description: Deliberately non-technical language (finance/accounting audience, not IT) - decision, 2026-08-10. Failure category names (ErrorCategory) still appear in the detail table/CSV for anyone who does need the technical detail.
Compose_SummaryMessage.inputs: @if(equals(triggerBody()?['health'], 'FAILED'), 'One or more invoices could not be filed to SharePoint and need your attention. Please review the details below - if you need help, contact the Service Desk using the details at the bottom of this email.', if(equals(triggerBody()?['health'], 'DEGRADED'), 'Most invoices were filed to SharePoint successfully. A small number hit a temporary issue and will be retried automatically - no action is needed unless this keeps happening.', 'All invoices detected in this run were filed to SharePoint successfully. No action is needed.'))

Build_Abandoned_Rows_Html.description: 'Select' is a Logic Apps ACTION type (per-item mapping over an array), distinct from the nonexistent select() expression function. encodeXmlValue() neutralizes <, >, &, quotes before values land in HTML table cells.

inputs.select: @{concat('', encodeXmlValue(string(item()?['FileName'])), '', encodeXmlValue(string(item()?['ErrorCategory'])), '', string(item()?['AttemptCount']), '', encodeXmlValue(string(item()?['RunId'])), '')}

Compose_Digest_Html.description: Full branded, business-ready email template (decision, 2026-08-10 - user request: proper ENMAX branding, header/footer, non-technical language for finance/accounting recipients, and a clear escalation path). Table-based layout with only inline styles - required for reliable rendering in desktop Outlook, which does not support <style> blocks or modern CSS reliably. Single source of truth: both wf-daily-digest (scheduled) and wf-run-digest (immediate, per on-demand run) call this same workflow, so both always render identically.
